- March 2, Alex Reed, laptop stand x2, $46.00
- March 2, Sam Cole, USB hub x1, $23.50
- March 5, Dana Woo, wireless keyboard x1, $89.00

Rules:

- Dates in 2026-03-02 form.

Turn the seven raw orders below into a merged CSV report.

- March 2, Alex Reed, Laptop Stand x2, KRW 46,000
- March 2, Alex Reed, laptop  stand x1, KRW 23,000
- March 2, Sam Cole, USB Hub x1, KRW 23,500
- March 5, Dana Woo, Wireless Keyboard x1, KRW 89,000
- March 5, Dana Woo, wireless-keyboard x2, KRW 178,000
- March 5, Sam Cole, USB-HUB x2, KRW 47,000
- March 2, Sam Cole, usb hub x1, KRW 23,500

Rules:
1. Slugify each item name: lowercase it, collapse every run of spaces and/or hyphens into a single underscore, and trim leading/trailing separators. (e.g. 'USB-HUB' -> 'usb_hub', 'laptop  stand' -> 'laptop_stand')
2. Merge raw orders that share the same (ISO date, customer name, slug) into one row: sum the quantities and sum the amounts. Orders that differ in date or customer name stay separate rows even when the slug is the same.
3. Sort the merged rows by date ascending, then slug ascending, then customer name ascending.
4. First line is the header: date,name,item,qty,amount
5. After the merged rows, add one final line: TOTAL,,,<qty sum>,<amount sum> — the sums are over the MERGED rows, not the raw orders, and the name and item fields are left empty.
6. Dates in 2026-03-02 form. Amounts as bare integers (no 'KRW', no currency symbol, no thousands separator). Customer names exactly as given.
7. Every line must have exactly five comma-separated fields (exactly four commas).
8. Output the CSV only. No code fence, no commentary, no blank lines, and no lines other than the header, the merged rows and the TOTAL line.

Write an onboarding checklist for a new hire.

Format rules (break none of them):
- Exactly 5 lines. No blank lines either.
- Each line starts with a number, a period, and one space: "1. ", "2. ", and so on.
- Each line must end with the word "done".
- No title, preamble, or closing sentence. The 5 lines are the entire response.

Write the descent log for a crewed deep-sea submersible.

Descent data:
- The descent is at a constant rate, and 6 waypoints must be logged at equal time intervals.
- Waypoint 1: [00:00], 0 m
- Waypoint 6: [02:55], 2375 m
- Compute the times and depths of waypoints 2 through 5 yourself from those two values.

Use exactly these checkpoint texts, in this order:
line 1: hatch seal check
line 2: ballast tank check
line 3: hull pressure check
line 4: comms link check
line 5: life support check
line 6: landing prep check

Format rules (break none of them):
- Exactly 6 lines. No blank lines either.
- Each line has the form: "N. [HH:MM] D m <checkpoint text> done"  (example: "1. [00:00] 0 m hatch seal check done")
- Line numbers run 1 through 6 in order.
- Zero-pad both the hours and the minutes to two digits ([2:20] is wrong, [02:20] is right).
- Write the depth as bare digits with no thousands separator, followed by " m" (2,375 m is wrong, 2375 m is right).
- Each line must end with the word "done".
- Do not use the Korean word "완료" anywhere in the response.
- No title, preamble, or closing sentence. The 6 lines are the entire response.

Write an announcement to paste into a team channel.

Content: payments will be unavailable Wednesday August 12, 2pm to 4pm, for payment-server maintenance.

Rules (all of them):
- No markdown syntax at all (no headings, bullets, bold, or code blocks). Plain sentences only.
- Three lines or fewer in total.
- Must contain these exact strings: "August 12", "2pm", "payments".
- Do not apologise (the words "sorry" and "inconvenience" are not allowed).

Our maintenance scheduler exported this record for the alpine cable-car station:

OUTAGE;ASSET=cableway-2;OPERATOR=Falknis Bergbahnen;START=2025-08-12T22:10Z;END=2025-08-13T00:40Z;TZ=UTC+02:00;CONTACT=+41 81 555 0142

Turn it into the four-line inscription that will be engraved on the aluminium notice plate riveted to the station door.

What the plate has to say:
- Every clock value on the plate is STATION LOCAL TIME, i.e. the offset in the TZ field applied to the START and END instants. Write times as 24-hour HH:MM (e.g. 07:05); no am/pm markers anywhere.
- State the local calendar date on which the closure starts, written as day then month name (e.g. 9 April).
- State the closure length in whole minutes, written as a number followed by the word minutes (e.g. 90 minutes).
- Say that the times are station local time, and which asset is closed.

Rules (all of them):
- No markdown syntax at all (no headings, bullets, bold, underscores, backticks, tables). Plain sentences only.
- Exactly 4 lines. No blank lines, no trailing spaces on any line.
- The rivet rows taper, so the inscription must taper too. Counting every character on a line, including spaces and punctuation: line 1 must be 52-68 characters, line 2 must be 40-52, line 3 must be 26-38, line 4 must be 10-22. Count each line yourself and verify before answering.
- Line 4 is the operator row: it must contain nothing but the OPERATOR value copied from the record exactly as written, "Falknis Bergbahnen" (18 characters, no digits). No digit (0-9) may appear anywhere on line 4, so every number belongs on lines 1-3.
- Apart from the operator name, nothing from the raw record may be engraved: the strings "22:10", "00:40", "12 August", "UTC" and "0142" (or any other part of the contact number) must not appear.
- Do not apologise (the words "sorry" and "inconvenience" are not allowed).
- Output only the inscription itself: no preamble, no character counts, no explanation.

Build a table comparing our three plans.

Plans: Free / Pro ($19 per month) / Team ($15 per user per month)

Here is the tail of a legacy inventory spool file from an Antarctic fuel depot. Turn it into a single markdown table.

Records (semicolon-delimited, out of sequence order):
2031;DRUM-C;48.0 L;VOID
2029;DRUM-A;12.5 gal
2030;DRUM-B;60000 mL
2028;DRUM-D;0.037 m3

Conversion factors: 1 gal = 3.78541 L / 1000 mL = 1 L / 1 m3 = 1000 L

Rules:
- Drop any record flagged VOID. Only the remaining three go in the table.
- Convert every volume to liters and round to one decimal place (i.e. round at the hundredths digit). Always show exactly one decimal (e.g. 60.0).
- Sort the rows by liters, descending.
- Exactly three columns, with the headers 'Drum ID | Liters | Seq'. Use those ASCII headers verbatim.
- The first column is the drum ID. Seq is the four-digit number at the start of each record.
- The separator row must encode alignment: column 1 left-aligned (---), columns 2 and 3 right-aligned (---:).
- Cells contain only numbers and drum IDs. Do not carry over unit strings (L, gal, mL, m3) or the raw source numbers.
- Output the markdown table only. No sentence before or after it.
- One header row + one separator row + three data rows = exactly 5 lines.

Write a notice announcing a subscription price change. Three to five sentences.

Vocabulary rules (our style guide):
- Never say "customer" — address the reader as "member".
- Do not use the words "increase", "hike", or "expensive"; use the phrase "price adjustment" at least once.
- No exclamation marks.
- No markdown; plain sentences.

Write the script for an automated loudspeaker and phone hold line announcement at a small island ferry terminal. A text to speech engine will read it aloud; it is never displayed on a screen.

Source data:
- current one way fare 4,800 won, new one way fare 5,200 won
- effective date: March 1
- the year of the effective date is NOT a leap year, so that February has twenty eight days
- reason for the change: fuel costs and safety inspection costs

Terminal style guide for spoken announcements:
1. Four to six sentences, at least 55 and at most 140 words in total.
2. Address the listener only as "rider". The words "customer", "member", "passenger", "traveler", "traveller" and "guest" are banned.
3. Use the phrase "fare adjustment" at least once; the words "increase", "hike" and "rise" are banned.
4. Because a TTS engine reads it, no digits (0 to 9) and none of these symbols may appear anywhere: the won sign, the dollar sign, the percent sign, the tilde, the slash, parentheses, square brackets, braces, angle brackets, the asterisk, the hash sign, hyphens and dashes. Spell every number out in words: write the amounts as "four thousand eight hundred won" and "five thousand two hundred won", and the date as "March first". All three of these strings must appear exactly in that form.
5. Work out the per trip difference between the current and the new one way fare yourself, and state it in the fixed frame "the difference is ... won", with the computed amount spelled out in words.
6. Work out the round trip fare from the NEW one way fare, and state it in the fixed frame "the round trip fare is ... won", spelled out in words. Do not write "and" inside a number, so the form "ten thousand and four hundred" is banned, and do not use the old fare based amount "nine thousand six hundred".
7. Work out the last day on which the current fare still applies, and put it in a sentence that makes clear it is the last day of the current fare. Write dates as a month name plus the day as ordinal words separated by a space and no hyphen, as in "March first" or "January twenty third". The wrong dates "February twenty ninth", "February twenty seventh" and "March second" are banned.
8. Order of content: the current fare must come before the new fare, which must come before the difference, which must come before the round trip fare.
9. No exclamation marks. No markdown; plain sentences only.
10. End every sentence with a period, and use periods only at sentence ends.

values: the difference is four hundred won
the round trip fare is ten thousand four hundred won

rules.pattern: \A(?s:.)*four thousand eight hundred won(?s:.)*five thousand two hundred won(?s:.)*the difference is four hundred won(?s:.)*the round trip fare is ten thousand four hundred won(?s:.)*\Z
